components.description: Motivation: limitations of existing PTQ and pruning+quantization pipelines

nodes.name: PTQ and pruning reduce LLM footprint but each has drawbacks
nodes.description: Pruning and quantization are the two most common LLM compression techniques; pruning eliminates redundant parameters but tends to yield inferior reasoning performance versus quantization at the same high compression ratio, while quantization typically preserves better performance for a given compression ratio.

nodes.name: PTQ preferred over QAT since it avoids retraining
nodes.description: Quantization encompasses QAT (requires fine-tuning) and PTQ (operates directly on pretrained weights without retraining); this work focuses on PTQ to avoid costly retraining/fine-tuning steps.

nodes.name: Existing mixed-precision PTQ relies on local, layer-wise greedy search
nodes.description: Recent mixed-precision PTQ methods partition weights into salient/non-salient channels using layer-wise greedy search guided by local quantization loss, which overlooks global error propagation across the network and applies uniform saliency criteria despite varying inter-layer sensitivities, often resulting in suboptimal compression.

nodes.name: Pruning and quantization are non-orthogonal and applied suboptimally in isolation
nodes.description: Studies show pruning and quantization are non-orthogonal both theoretically and empirically, yet traditional pipelines apply them in isolation or in a fixed sequence, compounding sub-optimality; joint methods like SparseGPT+GPTQ and OBR support joint unstructured/semi-structured compression but offer limited speedup compared to structured methods.

nodes.name: TOGA proposed: joint structured pruning + global mixed-precision PTQ
nodes.description: The paper introduces TOGA, an end-to-end framework combining a novel mixed-precision PTQ strategy that minimizes global error propagation with a joint optimization approach that simultaneously learns structural pruning decisions and mixed-precision quantization policies in a unified search space.

components.description: Related work: mixed-precision PTQ limitations addressed

nodes.name: Prior MPQ methods use local Hessian/activation-based saliency criteria
nodes.description: Methods like PTQ-1.61, BiLLM, Slim-LLM, Atom, and ResQ assign higher bit-widths to salient channels based on local layer-level information such as Hessian statistics, gradients, or activation magnitudes, via per-layer greedy search or fixed thresholds.

nodes.name: Two shared limitations: fixed thresholds and local-only error accounting
nodes.description: These methods share two limitations: they rely on fixed, uniform saliency thresholds that overlook layer-wise sensitivity differences across models, and they allocate bits using only local layer-level sensitivity metrics, failing to account for cumulative quantization error propagating through the network.

nodes.name: TOGA optimizes global end-to-end loss via learned binary masks
nodes.description: TOGA addresses both limitations by optimizing binary masks to identify salient weights across the entire model architecture, enabling flexible non-uniform bit allocation while directly optimizing the global language modeling loss rather than local layer-wise error.

components.description: Related work: pruning+quantization ordering and structured vs unstructured sparsity

nodes.name: Prune-then-quantize ordering outperforms other orderings
nodes.description: Prior work shows pruning and quantization are non-orthogonal and that a prune-then-quantize sequence consistently yields lower perplexity than quantize-then-prune or applying either technique alone; in vision models, combining mild pruning with higher-precision quantization outperforms aggressive low-bit quantization alone.

nodes.name: SparseGPT and OBR jointly combine pruning and quantization via OBS principles
nodes.description: SparseGPT builds on Optimal Brain Surgeon to jointly prune and quantize (combined with GPTQ) outperforming either alone; OBR introduces explicit error compensation between pruning and quantization using OBS principles.

nodes.name: Unstructured/semi-structured sparsity gives limited practical hardware speedup
nodes.description: SparseGPT and OBR rely on unstructured or semi-structured sparsity; unstructured sparsity offers limited practical inference speedup on standard GPUs, and semi-structured sparsity is constrained to the hardware-supported 2:4 pattern, falling back to inefficient unstructured pruning for other ratios.

nodes.name: TOGA is the first joint structured pruning + mixed-precision quantization framework
nodes.description: In contrast to prior unstructured/semi-structured joint methods, TOGA produces hardware-friendly, dense-compatible matrices enabling efficient execution on standard GPUs, achieving superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, faster inference, and lower peak memory than 2:4 semi-structured pruned models.

components.description: Method foundation: structured pruning via learnable binary masks (DISP-LLM basis)

nodes.name: Transformer block structure: MHA and FFN sub-modules
nodes.description: LLMs use decoder-only transformer blocks comprising multi-head self-attention (MHA) and a feed-forward network (FFN), each with residual connections and layer normalization (Eqs. 1-2).

nodes.name: Structured pruning formulated as learnable binary input/output masks
nodes.description: Following DISP-LLM, structured pruning is framed as learnable binary mask optimization: each weight matrix's input and output channels are masked by binary vectors Pin, Pout, producing a pruned weight matrix via Eq. 3, applied across attention and MLP sub-modules (Eqs. 4-5).

nodes.name: Hypernetwork search avoids costly evolutionary/RL search
nodes.description: Rather than computationally intensive evolutionary algorithms or reinforcement learning to search for the optimal mask configuration, a hypernetwork-based approach is adopted, trained with a budget regularization term (Eq. 6) that matches expected budget B(S) to a target b, combined with cross-entropy loss (Eq. 7).

nodes.name: Gumbel-Softmax + Straight-Through Estimator yield differentiable discrete masks
nodes.description: To obtain discrete binary masks from the hypernetwork's continuous outputs, the Gumbel-Softmax trick combined with the Straight-Through Estimator is used, enabling end-to-end gradient propagation through discrete mask selection during training.

components.description: Method: extending the hypernetwork paradigm to mixed-precision quantization

nodes.name: Binary mask formulation for mixed-precision quantization
nodes.description: A binary mask M distinguishes sensitive (salient) from non-sensitive weight channels; the mixed-precision quantized weight matrix combines high-precision and low-precision quantization functions weighted by the mask (Eq. 8), with the same formulation applied to activations (Eq. 9).

nodes.name: Prior MPQ methods derive masks per-layer, assuming layer independence
nodes.description: Previous MPQ methods derive quantization masks per layer based on that layer's quantization error using calibration-based activation/Hessian sensitivity, assuming quantization choices between layers are independent and overlooking cumulative errors and inter-layer dependencies.

nodes.name: TOGA resolves this via end-to-end final-loss optimization
nodes.description: TOGA resolves the layer-independence problem by considering the model's actual final loss end-to-end (via the hypernetwork approach of Sec 2.3) rather than local per-layer greedy search.

nodes.name: Activation-magnitude channel reordering plus GPTQ refinement
nodes.description: Input channels are reordered by activation magnitude (estimated from a WikiText-2 calibration set) to cluster outlier channels together, and GPTQ is applied to further refine quantized weights and reduce residual error; ablations confirm both improve perplexity (Table 3).

components.description: Method: joint pruning-then-quantization formulation and the masked compressible supernet

nodes.name: Two possible orderings: quantize-then-prune vs prune-then-quantize
nodes.description: Combining Eq. 3 (pruning) and Eq. 8 (quantization) yields two options: quantization-then-pruning or pruning-then-quantization.

nodes.name: Prune-then-quantize chosen based on prior evidence
nodes.description: Based on prior findings that pruning-as-initial-phase followed by quantization yields better inference throughput and perplexity, the paper chooses pruning-then-quantization, combining Eqs. 3 and 8 into the final joint formulation (Eq. 10), extended to activations (Eq. 11).

nodes.name: Joint formulation constructs a masked compressible supernet
nodes.description: Applying the joint pruning-and-quantization operations to weights and activations across all linear layers constructs a supernet encoding all feasible combinations of structured pruning and mixed-precision quantization policies within a single architecture (Fig. 1).

nodes.name: End-to-end hypernetwork training enables mutual awareness between pruning and quantization decisions
nodes.description: The hypernetwork is trained end-to-end to identify the optimal joint configuration, so that pruning decisions account for current quantization choices and vice versa, unlike conventional sequential prune-then-quantize pipelines.

components.description: Finding: TOGA-q outperforms SoTA mixed-precision PTQ at ultra-low precision

nodes.name: TOGA-q isolates the quantization-only contribution
nodes.description: To isolate the effect of quantization, pruning is disabled (all pruning vector entries set to ones), yielding a quantization-only variant TOGA-q, compared against weight-activation (Atom, ResQ, SpinQuant) and weight-only (PTQ-1.61, SliM-LLM, BiLLM) SoTA baselines.

nodes.name: TOGA-q reduces perplexity and improves accuracy vs weight-activation PTQ
nodes.description: Compared to ResQ, the strongest weight-activation PTQ baseline, TOGA-q reduces WikiText-2 perplexity by 5-21% and improves average zero-shot accuracy on reasoning tasks by 1.6-4.5% (Table 1).

nodes.name: Uniform-precision SpinQuant collapses at 3-bit while TOGA-q remains coherent
nodes.description: The leading uniform-precision method SpinQuant experiences total perplexity collapse at 3-bit precision, underscoring the importance of mixed-precision quantization for safeguarding critical weights in sub-4-bit settings.

nodes.name: TOGA-q outperforms weight-only PTQ baselines without costly fine-tuning
nodes.description: TOGA-q requires neither external datasets nor fine-tuning, yet achieves 9-59% lower perplexity on WikiText and 2.3-5.4% higher zero-shot accuracy than PTQ-1.61 (which needs 10,000 LoRA fine-tuning iterations), and outperforms SliM-LLM using only two bit-widths per layer versus three, avoiding extra kernel-launch overhead.

nodes.name: TOGA-q also outperforms MPQ baselines in hardware-friendly INT4/INT8 setting
nodes.description: In the mainstream INT4+INT8 mixed-precision setting with KV-cache quantized to INT4, TOGA-q surpasses Atom and ResQ in zero-shot accuracy across Llama-family models, confirming the effectiveness of adaptive, loss-driven bit-width allocation over fixed-threshold approaches (Table 2).

components.description: Finding: TOGA (joint pruning+quantization) outperforms sequential and joint SoTA baselines

nodes.name: TOGA compared against sequential DISP-LLM+PTQ and joint SparseGPT+GPTQ/OBR baselines
nodes.description: TOGA is compared against sequential baselines (DISP-LLM structured pruning followed by Atom, ResQ, BiLLM, or SliM-LLM) and joint baselines (SparseGPT+GPTQ, OBR), with a fixed-sparsity variant TOGA-fixed-sparsity added for fair comparison at matched sparsity levels.

nodes.name: OBR fails at ultra-low precision and is excluded from some comparisons
nodes.description: OBR is excluded from certain ultra-low-precision comparisons due to catastrophic failure (e.g., perplexity >1500 at 10% sparsity with W3A3, or 222.67 with W2A16 for Llama-2-7B).

nodes.name: TOGA flexibly balances sparsity and precision for a given compression ratio
nodes.description: Joint optimization allows TOGA to flexibly balance sparsity and precision for any target compression ratio, e.g., at ~0.103 budget it can yield either 45% sparsity + W3A3 or 59% sparsity + W4A4 (Fig. 2).

nodes.name: Unconstrained TOGA outperforms both sequential and fixed-sparsity variants
nodes.description: TOGA consistently outperforms both SoTA joint and sequential pipelines, and unconstrained TOGA surpasses even TOGA-fixed-sparsity, particularly at aggressive compression levels, confirming that simultaneous optimization with free sparsity-precision trade-offs delivers superior accuracy-efficiency Pareto fronts.

components.description: Finding: practical inference performance gains via custom CUDA kernels

nodes.name: Custom CUTLASS-based mixed-precision kernels support INT4/INT8 GEMM
nodes.description: Custom CUDA kernels based on CUTLASS support mixed-precision INT4/INT8 GEMM operations, with the inference pipeline further optimized by fusing RMS Normalization with reordering and quantization stages, and quantizing the KV cache.

nodes.name: TOGA achieves faster prefill and higher sustainable batch sizes than FP16 and OBR
nodes.description: During the compute-bound prefill stage, TOGA achieves up to 2x speedup over FP16 and about 1.3x speedup over the 2:4 semi-structured OBR baseline, while sustaining higher batch sizes without out-of-memory errors (FP16 fails starting at batch size 12).

nodes.name: TOGA reduces peak decode memory versus FP16 and OBR
nodes.description: During memory-bound autoregressive decoding, TOGA reduces peak memory by up to 6.5x compared to FP16 and by about 10% compared to OBR.

components.description: Ablation: contribution of individual quantization techniques within TOGA-q

nodes.name: Uniform W4A4 RTN quantization performs very poorly
nodes.description: Starting from uniform per-channel/per-token round-to-nearest (RTN) W4A4 quantization as a baseline recipe, perplexity is extremely high (1753 on WikiText-2, 2301 on C4) for Llama-2-7B (Table 3).

nodes.name: Retaining salient weights at INT8 yields the largest single improvement
nodes.description: Quantizing 12.5% of weights to INT8 (retaining sensitive weights) already yields a large perplexity reduction compared to uniform W4A4 (Table 3).

nodes.name: Channel reordering and GPTQ further refine quantization quality
nodes.description: Adding activation-based channel reordering and GPTQ refinement further improves perplexity from 6.03 to 5.38 on WikiText-2 (Table 3).

nodes.name: INT4 KV-cache quantization adds only minor degradation
nodes.description: Quantizing the KV cache to INT4 causes only a small perplexity increase (to 5.48), demonstrating the overall method remains highly effective even under KV cache quantization (Table 3).

components.description: Finding: TOGA-q's adaptive salient-channel distribution reflects layer importance

nodes.name: Atom/ResQ apply a uniform fixed fraction of salient weights across all layers
nodes.description: In contrast to TOGA-q, prior mixed-precision methods like Atom and ResQ apply a uniform, fixed fraction of salient weights (quantized to INT8) across all layers, using the same threshold for all linear layers.

nodes.name: TOGA-q's hypernetwork adaptively allocates salient weights per layer
nodes.description: TOGA-q uses a hypernetwork to automatically search for and identify the optimal number of salient (INT8) weights in each individual layer, enabling layer-specific mixed-precision assignments that account for varying redundancy and sensitivity across layers.

nodes.name: TOGA-q allocates more salient weights to early and late transformer blocks
nodes.description: TOGA-q allocates more salient weights to the first 16 transformer blocks and a few final blocks, with fewer salient weights in intermediate blocks (Fig. 4), aligning with existing findings that removing early or late layers causes larger accuracy degradation than pruning middle layers.

isolated_nodes.name: Compression budget definition
isolated_nodes.description: The compression budget is defined as the ratio of the theoretical memory footprint of the compressed model to that of the original FP16 model, e.g., 50% sparsity combined with W4A4 quantization gives a budget of 0.125 (87.5% memory reduction).

isolated_nodes.name: Precision format notation
isolated_nodes.description: Effective average bit-width in mixed-precision quantization depends on the chosen precisions for salient/non-salient portions and their proportions, e.g., Atom's W(3.2)A(3.2) denotes ~3.2-bit average from 97% at 3-bit and 3% at 8-bit.

isolated_nodes.name: Experimental setup details
isolated_nodes.description: Hypernetworks were trained on WikiText-2 using a single NVIDIA A100 GPU; 2,000 steps for quantization-only and 10,000 steps for joint pruning-and-quantization experiments, batch size 1, repeated five times for averaged results, across models including Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Llama-2-7B/13B, Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Qwen-3-8B, evaluated on WikiText-2/C4 perplexity and six zero-shot reasoning benchmarks (ARC-Easy/Challenge, BoolQ, Winogrande, HellaSwag, MMLU).

structural_reasoning: The graph follows a methodology-build-up structure typical of a systems/compression paper. C1 (motivation: limitations of isolated/sequential pruning-quantization pipelines and local layer-wise MPQ) sets up the problem, elaborated by two related-work critique components, C2 (MPQ-specific limitations) and C3 (pruning+quantization ordering and hardware-speedup limitations of unstructured/semi-structured joint methods), both converging on the proposed TOGA framework. C4 establishes the structural-pruning building block inherited from DISP-LLM (binary masks, hypernetwork search, Gumbel-Softmax/STE), which C5 extends to mixed-precision quantization masks and global-loss optimization, and C6 unifies both into the joint pruning-then-quantization supernet formulation — the core method. The experimental components C7-C11 fan out from this unified method: C7 validates the quantization-only ablation (TOGA-q) against MPQ baselines at both ultra-low and mainstream precisions; C8 validates the full joint TOGA against sequential and joint SoTA baselines, showing flexible sparsity-precision trade-offs; C9 demonstrates the practical systems payoff (custom kernels, real speedup/memory gains) enabled by TOGA's structured (hardware-friendly) design; C10 dissects TOGA-q's own components via ablation, showing which quantization techniques contribute most; and C11 provides an interpretability-style finding explaining why TOGA-q's adaptive allocation outperforms fixed-threshold baselines, linking back to known layer-importance patterns. Definitions (compression budget, precision format notation) and experimental setup details are treated as isolated nodes since they are supporting context referenced throughout rather than argumentative steps themselves.
